title: Silicon modulator exceeding 110 GHz using tunable time-frequency equalization
abstract: This paper presents a silicon modulator that exceeds 110 GHz using a tunable time-frequency equalization technique, achieving the highest bandwidth and maximum baud rate without digital signal processing in an all-silicon modulator.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content: Imagine a high-speed internet connection that can transmit data at incredible speeds. To achieve this, we need electro-optic modulators that can convert electrical signals into optical signals. Silicon photonics is a promising technology for this, but it has limitations. Our research overcomes these limitations using a tunable time-frequency equalization technique.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: Our silicon modulator uses a series push-pull configuration with two PN junctions connected in series. The modulator has a main modulation region, a forward modulation region, a velocity mismatch region, and a reverse modulation region. The tunable time-frequency equalization technique allows us to optimize the modulator's performance.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: Our silicon modulator achieved a 3 dB bandwidth of 110 GHz and supported 140 Gbaud OOK modulation without digital signal processing. This represents the highest bandwidth and maximum baud rate achieved without digital signal processing in an all-silicon modulator.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: Our research has significant implications for the development of high-speed internet connections. By overcoming the limitations of silicon photonics, we can create faster and more efficient modulators that can transmit data at incredible speeds.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: Our research introduces a tunable time-frequency equalization technique that allows us to optimize the modulator's performance. This technique enables us to achieve higher bandwidths and baud rates than previously possible.

sections.title: What Came Next
sections.content: Our research opens up new possibilities for the development of high-speed internet connections. Future work can focus on further optimizing the modulator's performance and exploring new applications for this technology.
